note: Prompts for evaluating or improving this skill later. Each run is a whole film, so they are expensive: run one at a time, and judge the result by watching it. Nothing here has been run.

evals.prompt: We have an ACL 2027 paper (PDF at ./paper.pdf, code in ./repo, site https://example.org/proj). Make an intro video of about three minutes for the conference and the site. English narration and English captions, plus a copy without captions. The project name is pronounced "Lumen". Check this machine first, and ask before any download.
evals.expected_output: Runs tools/doctor.mjs and asks before any download; collects numbers into js/data.js with their tables; writes a script with a promise, a slogan, a fence, a question, a surprise and a closing sentence; lays in a voice with --as-plan before timing scenes; delivers out/<slug>.mp4 and out/<slug>_captions_en.mp4 with narration; reports verification in numbers and says what could not be verified (hearing).

evals.prompt: (Three screenshots attached.) Figure 1: the venue name on the title card is too small; write it out in full. Figure 2: this screen has too many words. Figure 3: replace the closing line with one sentence that says what the work is. Leave the rest as it is.
evals.expected_output: Archives the current version first; changes only the three things (venue written out with the abbreviation in brackets and enlarged; the dense screen split or replaced by a concrete picture; the end card reduced to one sentence in the statement type that comes up as it is spoken); re-renders; reports what changed and whether the length changed; mentions anything extended beyond the three notes.

evals.prompt: The narration voice sounds too young for this. Can you switch to a male voice, and slow it down a little? Keep everything else.
evals.expected_output: Offers or writes short audition samples of a few male Kokoro voices (cannot judge them itself) or picks one and says so; re-synthesises with a lower --speed and/or longer pauses without --as-plan; rebuilds cue sheet, bed and render so captions and pictures follow the new voice; reports the new length and that nothing was cut; asks the user to listen.

evals.prompt: Add the existing ECCV film as an example in this skill, but do not publish the original footage of people, and do not change the uploaded MP4. Check the video entry on the site and in the README.
evals.expected_output: Adds an explicitly labelled teaching adaptation with placeholders and ownership notes; preserves the frozen film; distinguishes paper claims, public-release output and source identities; checks covers independently; uses a click-to-load website player and an image link in README; asks before publishing.

evals.prompt: The build finished, but some transitions have thin lines, the arrow looks wrong, and YouTube does not show chapters. Diagnose without global installs.
evals.expected_output: Runs the page, encoded-pixel and glyph-font audits; inspects flagged timestamps rather than hiding them; validates 0:00, at least three chapters and minimum 10 seconds; reports decoded AAC true peak or explicitly says it was not measured; uses existing or approved project-local tools.
